title: WORKSHEET 51
subject: Gerund or Infinitive
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 51: Gerund or Infinitive

sections.instruction: Use the GERUND to connect the following: (Example: Peter's sometimes late. He can't help it. → Peter can't help being late.)

questions.prompt: Gordon has to get up early. He dislikes it.
acceptedAnswers: Gordon dislikes getting up early.
Gordon dislikes having to get up early.

questions.prompt: Paul asked Mary to come home. He remembers it.
acceptedAnswers: Paul remembers asking Mary to come home.
Paul remembers having asked Mary to come home.

questions.prompt: Jill occasionally speaks Spanish. She can't avoid it.
acceptedAnswers: Jill can't avoid speaking Spanish occasionally.
Jill can't avoid occasionally speaking Spanish.
Jill can't avoid speaking Spanish.

questions.prompt: Jim didn't take his holiday until June. He delayed it.
acceptedAnswers: Jim delayed taking his holiday until June.

questions.prompt: Jim was speaking French when Bob came in. He stopped.
acceptedAnswers: Jim stopped speaking French when Bob came in.

questions.prompt: Jim wanted to see the race. He didn't want to miss it.
acceptedAnswers: Jim didn't want to miss seeing the race.

questions.prompt: You may have an accident if you drive that car. You risk it.
acceptedAnswers: You risk having an accident if you drive that car.

questions.prompt: I wouldn't like to work in an office. I don't fancy it.
acceptedAnswers: I don't fancy working in an office.

questions.prompt: I spent all my money. I regret it, because I've got none left now.
acceptedAnswers: I regret spending all my money.
I regret having spent all my money.
I regret spending all my money because I've got none left now.
I regret having spent all my money because I've got none left now.
questions.explanation: regret + -ing = be sorry about a past action

questions.prompt: Henry has his lunch very late. He is used to it.
acceptedAnswers: Henry is used to having his lunch very late.
Henry is used to having lunch very late.

questions.prompt: John saw the girl. He denies it.
acceptedAnswers: John denies seeing the girl.
John denies having seen the girl.

questions.prompt: I had dinner with a film star. I'll never forget it.
acceptedAnswers: I'll never forget having dinner with a film star.
I'll never forget having had dinner with a film star.
questions.explanation: never forget + -ing = recall a past event

questions.prompt: Richard took the books home with him. He admitted it.
acceptedAnswers: Richard admitted taking the books home with him.
Richard admitted having taken the books home with him.

questions.prompt: Mary wanted to have dinner at a restaurant. She suggested it.
acceptedAnswers: Mary suggested having dinner at a restaurant.

questions.prompt: You should speak English all the time. You should practise it.
acceptedAnswers: You should practise speaking English all the time.
You should practice speaking English all the time.

sections.instruction: Complete the sentences using the GERUND (after prepositions):

questions.prompt: David is studying. He's bored.
acceptedAnswers: David is bored with studying.
David is bored of studying.

questions.prompt: Gordon likes to watch football. He's keen.
acceptedAnswers: Gordon is keen on watching football.

questions.prompt: Peter wants to learn English. He's interested.
acceptedAnswers: Peter is interested in learning English.

questions.prompt: Sheila keeps her own room tidy. She's responsible.
acceptedAnswers: Sheila is responsible for keeping her own room tidy.

questions.prompt: Sally will visit her aunt. She's excited.
acceptedAnswers: Sally is excited about visiting her aunt.

questions.prompt: Swan will meet Gordon. She is looking forward.
acceptedAnswers: Swan is looking forward to meeting Gordon.

questions.prompt: Paul doesn't want to be misunderstood. He's afraid.
acceptedAnswers: Paul is afraid of being misunderstood.

questions.prompt: Jane has to do the housework by herself. She's tired.
acceptedAnswers: Jane is tired of doing the housework by herself.
Jane is tired of having to do the housework by herself.

questions.prompt: John has to get up early. He is used.
acceptedAnswers: John is used to getting up early.

questions.prompt: Tom passed all his exams. He succeeded.
acceptedAnswers: Tom succeeded in passing all his exams.

sections.instruction: Supply an appropriate form, GERUND or INFINITIVE, of the verbs in parentheses:

questions.prompt: Mary reminded me [gap] (be / not) late for the meeting.
acceptedAnswers: not to be

questions.prompt: We went for a walk after we finished [gap] (clean) up the kitchen.
acceptedAnswers: cleaning

questions.prompt: When do you expect [gap] (leave) on your trip?
acceptedAnswers: to leave

questions.prompt: The baby started [gap] (talk) when she was about eighteen months old.
acceptedAnswers: talking|to talk

questions.prompt: I'm getting tired. I need [gap] (take) a break.
acceptedAnswers: to take

questions.prompt: I've decided [gap] (stay) here over vacation and [gap] (paint) my room.
acceptedAnswers: to stay / paint|to paint

questions.prompt: Sometimes students avoid [gap] (look) at the teacher if they don't want [gap] (answer) a question.
acceptedAnswers: looking / to answer

questions.prompt: The travel agent advised us [gap] (not / wait) until August.
acceptedAnswers: not to wait

questions.prompt: We're going out for dinner. Would you like [gap] (join) us?
acceptedAnswers: to join

questions.prompt: Mrs. Allen promised [gap] (come) tomorrow.
acceptedAnswers: to come

questions.prompt: My boss expects me [gap] (complete) this work as soon as possible.
acceptedAnswers: to complete

questions.prompt: Even though I asked the people in front of me at the movie [gap] (be) quiet, they kept [gap] (talk).
acceptedAnswers: to be / talking

questions.prompt: Joan and David were considering [gap] (get) married in June, but they finally decided [gap] (wait) until August.
acceptedAnswers: getting / to wait

questions.prompt: He doesn't mind [gap] (be) alone.
acceptedAnswers: being

questions.prompt: The teacher seems [gap] (be) in a good mood today.
acceptedAnswers: to be

questions.prompt: Mrs. Jackson warned her young son [gap] (not / touch) the hot stove.
acceptedAnswers: not to touch

questions.prompt: Jack advised me [gap] (rent) a new apartment.
acceptedAnswers: to rent

questions.prompt: His teacher encourages him [gap] (study) harder.
acceptedAnswers: to study

questions.prompt: Lucy pretended [gap] (know) the answer to my question.
acceptedAnswers: to know

questions.prompt: Could you please stop [gap] (make) so much noise?
acceptedAnswers: making

questions.prompt: He doesn't let anyone [gap] (smoke) in his office.
acceptedAnswers: smoke
